source_text: Resistance was particularly high against all pyrethroids, with very low mortality rates for permethrin (type I; ♀ 13 ± 5.3 % mortality)
whereas high resistance was observed against the non-ester pyrethroid etofenprox with no mortality.
Similarly, this population is highly resistant to the carbamates bendiocarb (♀ 30.1 ± 5.1 % mortality)
Unlike in 2009, it is now resistant to DDT (♀ 69.9 ± 5.7 % mortality)
However, it remains fully susceptible to organophosphates, with 100 % mortality for fenitrothion
The PBO synergist assay revealed a high recovery of susceptibility to DDT after pre-exposure for 1 h to PBO (♀ 95.9 ± 3 %; ♂ 97.30 ± 1.2 % mortality)
Anopheles arabiensis females were highly resistant to the pyrethroid permethrin (♀ 14.3 % mortality)
and moderately resistant to the organochlorine DDT (♀ 87.5 % mortality),
but fully susceptible to the carbamate bendiocarb (♀ 100 % mortality) (Fig. 3b).
